headline: Israel is building a nearly 90km network of military roads and outposts across southern Lebanon, satellite imagery shows
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the network] Israel is building roads and military outposts across southern Lebanon, with satellite imagery showing a network spanning nearly 90km, according to Al Jazeera's video report from Baraachit (Zeina Khodr, published Nov 7 16:29Z). The report shows ~50km of new roads…
sources: Al Jazeera video report (Zeina Khodr reporting from Baraachit, southern Lebanon)
fault_line: Entrenchment or security -- is Israel building a permanent new border in Lebanon, or a buffer it will trade away?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the network] Israel is building roads and military outposts across southern Lebanon, with satellite imagery showing a network spanning nearly 90km, according to Al Jazeera's video report from Baraachit (Zeina Khodr, published Nov 7 16:29Z). The report shows ~50km of new roads linking outposts on hills and bypassing now-empty, destroyed Lebanese villages. [CORROBORATED -- the entrenchment pattern] L'Orient-Le Jour's satellite-imagery investigation (Nov 2-3) documented the same construction and estimates Israel currently occupies more than 600 sq km of southern Lebanon; Lebanon's National News Agency reported Nov 1 (via Arab News) that Israeli forces are building roads through mountains and valleys in the western and central sectors to connect military positions, with demolition operations under way. Misbar's Sentinel-2 analysis (Nov 7) independently tracked a new mountain road along the Litani from Oct 1-11 imagery. [ANALYSIS -- intent] That the network points to a 'prolonged' Israeli military presence is the reporting outlets' interpretation (AJ, L'Orient-Le Jour); no Israeli official comment on the roads or on intent is on record. [CONTEXT] The construction follows US-sponsored Lebanon-Israel military/technical talks in Tampa, Florida, Oct 20-21, which ended without agreement.
sections.what_verified: AJ's own satellite-imagery reporting (T2) + L'Orient-Le Jour investigation (T3) + NNA via Arab News (T3) = 3 distinct tiered families on the construction itself. Misbar (no declared tier) is attribution only. The 'prolonged presence' reading is analysis, not a confirmed Israeli intent.
sections.what_disputed: No Israeli official statement on the roads or their purpose is on record; the 'prolonged presence' framing is the outlets' interpretation. Misbar notes its Oct 1-11 imagery could not establish whether the Litani-road excavation was connected to the newly built road, or exactly when work began (cloud cover).
sections.why_matters: 90 kilometres of new roads -- the map of a stay, not a raid. Satellite imagery shows the network; Israel has not commented. The roads bypass destroyed villages and link hilltop outposts -- a new line drawn on the ground while talks stall.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (AJ video report published 2026-11-07T16:29Z = 20:29 ; zero '90km'/'roads' mentions in any Nov 6 or Nov 7 scan -- grep confirms) -- Israel is building a nearly 90km network of military roads and outposts across southern Lebanon, satellite imagery shows; ~50km newly built; concerns over a prolonged military presence

totw_analysis: Our read: 90 kilometres of new roads -- the map of a stay, not a raid. Satellite imagery shows the network; Israel has not commented. The roads bypass destroyed villages and link hilltop outposts -- a new line drawn on the ground while talks stall. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Entrenchment or security -- is Israel building a permanent new border in Lebanon, or a buffer it will trade away?
